cards.front: habitat
cards.back: The place where a plant or animal lives.
cards.say: habitat. The place where a plant or animal lives. A pond is a habitat.

cards.front: adaptation
cards.back: A feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat.
cards.say: adaptation. A feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat. Webbed feet are an adaptation for swimming.

cards.front: environment
cards.back: Everything around a living thing, such as air, water, soil and other living things.
cards.say: environment. Everything around a living thing, such as air, water, soil and other living things. A desert is a hot, dry environment.

cards.front: survive
cards.back: To stay alive.
cards.say: survive. To stay alive. Plants need water to survive.

cards.front: Name a habitat.
cards.back: A pond, a forest, a desert, a coral reef or a rainforest.
cards.say: Name a habitat. A pond, a forest, a desert, a coral reef or a rainforest.

cards.front: Why does a camel have a hump?
cards.back: It stores fat, which gives energy when food is hard to find in the desert.
cards.say: Why does a camel have a hump? It stores fat, which gives energy when food is hard to find in the desert.

cards.front: Why does a polar bear have thick fur?
cards.back: To keep it warm in the cold Arctic.
cards.say: Why does a polar bear have thick fur? To keep it warm in the cold Arctic.

cards.front: Why is a polar bear white?
cards.back: White fur helps it hide on the snow and ice.
cards.say: Why is a polar bear white? White fur helps it hide on the snow and ice.

cards.front: Why do fish have gills?
cards.back: Gills let them take in oxygen from the water.
cards.say: Why do fish have gills? Gills let them take in oxygen from the water.

cards.front: Why does a cactus have a thick stem?
cards.back: It stores water for a dry desert.
cards.say: Why does a cactus have a thick stem? It stores water for a dry desert.

cards.front: Why do cacti have spines instead of leaves?
cards.back: Spines lose less water and protect the plant from animals.
cards.say: Why do cacti have spines instead of leaves? Spines lose less water and protect the plant from animals.

cards.front: camouflage
cards.back: Colours or patterns that help an animal blend in with its surroundings.
cards.say: camouflage. Colours or patterns that help an animal blend in with its surroundings. A chameleon uses camouflage.

cards.front: Why is a stick insect hard to see?
cards.back: It looks like a twig, so predators miss it.
cards.say: Why is a stick insect hard to see? It looks like a twig, so predators miss it.

cards.front: Why do ducks have webbed feet?
cards.back: Webbed feet help them swim.
cards.say: Why do ducks have webbed feet? Webbed feet help them swim.

cards.front: Why do birds in cold places have thick feathers?
cards.back: Thick feathers trap warm air to keep them warm.
cards.say: Why do birds in cold places have thick feathers? Thick feathers trap warm air to keep them warm.

cards.front: Why does a frog live near water?
cards.back: It needs moist skin and lays eggs in water.
cards.say: Why does a frog live near water? It needs moist skin and lays eggs in water.

cards.front: Which animal is adapted to cold, a polar bear or a camel?
cards.back: A polar bear.
cards.say: Which animal is adapted to cold, a polar bear or a camel? A polar bear.

cards.front: Which animal is adapted to desert life, a camel or a seal?
cards.back: A camel.
cards.say: Which animal is adapted to desert life, a camel or a seal? A camel.

cards.front: Name one way people can harm a habitat.
cards.back: For example, cutting down trees, pollution or building on wild land.
cards.say: Name one way people can harm a habitat. For example, cutting down trees, pollution or building on wild land.

cards.front: Name one way people can help a habitat.
cards.back: For example, planting trees, cleaning up litter or protecting wild areas.
cards.say: Name one way people can help a habitat. For example, planting trees, cleaning up litter or protecting wild areas.

cards.front: deforestation
cards.back: Cutting down large areas of forest.
cards.say: deforestation. Cutting down large areas of forest. Deforestation destroys the homes of animals.

cards.front: pollution
cards.back: Harmful things in the air, water or land.
cards.say: pollution. Harmful things in the air, water or land. Rubbish in a river is pollution.

cards.front: What happens to animals when their habitat is destroyed?
cards.back: They lose food and shelter and may die or move away.
cards.say: What happens to animals when their habitat is destroyed? They lose food and shelter and may die or move away.

cards.front: What is a nature reserve?
cards.back: A protected area where wildlife can live safely.
cards.say: What is a nature reserve? A protected area where wildlife can live safely.

cards.front: True or false: A living thing can live happily in any habitat.
cards.back: False. Each living thing is adapted to its own habitat.
cards.say: True or false: A living thing can live happily in any habitat. False. Each living thing is adapted to its own habitat.
